reasoning:
I tried to kill this three ways and it survived all three, and the mechanism is worse than the finding stated.

(1) Reproduction re-ran exactly: 627 rank / 654 tier / 135 value divergences, 786 divergent rows in the union, Conklin 469/1450 -> 666/1142, isCustomized:false on both. Numbers match the finding to the digit.

(2) My best kill attempt was that the finding mis-blamed the multiplier VALUE. Both responses report tepMultiplier=1.15 (GET tepMultiplierSource='default', POST 'override'), so a naive reading says nothing should change. I probed with an EMPTY body ({}) and got a byte-identical board — 0 rank, 0 tier, 0 value diffs. So the divergence is caused by the PRESENCE of the explicit key, not its value: posting the exact number the contract already reports as its default reprices 786 rows. That is the finding's stated root cause, empirically sharper than it stated.

(3) Code path is live and the gate is explicit: src/api/data_contract.py:6939 `if not tep_multiplier_is_override:` wraps the whole ADR-015 basis-conversion setup, so te_basis_conversion stays False for any explicit slider value and line 7690 falls through to `value * effective_non_tep_multiplier` — the flat 1.15 ADR-015 retired. tep_multiplier_source is set to 'override' at :9050 for any non-None value and threaded at :9187/:9211.

(4) The stock frontend really does post it. frontend/components/useSettings.js:35 `tepMultiplier: 1.15` is SETTINGS_DEFAULTS, and readSettings() at :176-188 actively MIGRATES a null/1.0/1.25 value up to 1.15 — so there is no path to the null 'auto' sentinel for a normal user. tepMultiplierIsCustomized (dynasty-data.js:919) returns true for any finite number, so fetchDynastyData takes the override branch on every load. Confirmed in a real browser with request interception per the topology rule: the only POST /api/* on a /rankings load is body {"tep_multiplier":1.15}.

(5) Confirmed at the pixel: the rendered table shows Bowers 9,876 and McBride 8,993 (delta board), while GET /api/data — which every server-side engine reads via latest_contract_data — has 9,947 and 9,264.

(6) Not fixed at HEAD (git log -L on 6937-6940 shows no change since the last automated refresh commit).

RESCOPE, one axis only: pagesAffected:1 is understated. 11 files under frontend/app (10 routes) call useDynastyData() and therefore render the tep-override board: /rankings, /trade, /arbitrage, /angle, /edge, /phases, /players/compare, /league, /idptc-rookies, /settings. The worst case is INSIDE /trade — frontend/app/trade/page.jsx:94 takes `rows` from useDynastyData (override board) while POST /api/trade/suggestions on the same page answers from latest_contract_data (GET board). The two boards disagree in one viewport. P0 stands and is if anything reinforced.

correctedBlastRadius.note: 786 = union of rows differing in rank, tier or value (627 rank / 654 tier / 135 value; value splits 82 TE, 50 PICK, 3 other), recounted independently. pagesAffected raised 1->10: every frontend/app page calling useDynastyData() renders the override board, including /trade, where the client board and the server engine disagree within one page.

whatWouldSettleIt: Already settled. If anyone wants to close it: make GET /api/data and the default POST body produce one board — either stop posting tep_multiplier when it equals the derived default, or stop letting an explicit value bypass the ADR-015 curve at data_contract.py:6939.

reasoning:
The defect is real and I could not break the reproduction. The severity is not.

CONFIRMED: (a) the probe re-ran and produced the stated numbers exactly; it drives the real library API (createDefaultWorkspace -> recordPick -> computeDraftStats), not a hand-built fixture. (b) The code has no budget clamp: draft-logic.js:734-748 computes theoreticalMaxBid from preDraft x aggression x combinedInflation x phaseMultiplier and myWinningBid = min(theoreticalMaxBid, topCompetitorMax + 1); myRemaining appears nowhere in that block (grep: myRemaining is used at :426, :524-528, :866, :974, :1032, :1897 — never in bid derivation). (c) :479-481 skips myTeamIdx when reducing effectiveBudgetByIdx, so effectiveBudgetFor is rival-only as claimed. (d) bidStatus (:2517-2537) classifies only against myWinningBid/enforceUpTo — 'Push up' at $24 on $4 cash reproduced. (e) The columns are live and user-facing: a real /draft load through request interception renders ENFORCE / WIN AT / MAX BID headers with dollar values. (f) 72 = default pool size, confirmed. (g) Not fixed at HEAD. (h) The modal warning at page.jsx:794-814 fires only on amt > myCeiling, so an unaffordable bid below the ceiling shows nothing — confirmed by reading the branch.

WHERE IT OVERSTATES — 'with no warning shown', which is the P0 bar in the protocol:
- page.jsx:250-254 renders 'My remaining' as a permanent card in the stats strip ABOVE the same table that shows Win at, with tooltip 'Starting $X - spent $Y'. The user is looking at $4 and $69 simultaneously. That is not a warning attached to the recommendation, but it is not a hidden or fabricated number either — nothing on screen tells the user they have more money than they do.
- The bid modal's simulator (page.jsx:838-841) shows 'My remaining before -> after' for the entered amount.
- The Target Board / par sheet carries a real budget-aware buffer (draft-logic.js:866, :974) that goes red when myRemaining cannot cover committed targets, described in the page's own help text at :3257 ('Short (red): buffer < 0 - you can't afford'). Opt-in, and not per-player, but it exists.
- The emitted number is not wrong under its own definition. myWinningBid is documented as 'the price that beats the field' (:741-743) and it correctly is that. The defect is a missing second clamp, not a miscomputation. No server-side value, trade price or ranking is wrong.

The genuinely misleading surfaces are bidStatus returning 'Push up' on an amount 6x the user's cash and nextBestTargets recommending targets they cannot fund — both real, both advice defects rather than a wrong number acted on blind. Downgrading to P1: reachable, live, ships bad advice in a common late-auction state, but the contradicting fact is on screen and nothing downstream of /draft is corrupted. Keeping this at P0 alongside W03-F001 (where the page and the trade engine serve different prices for the same asset with no contradicting number anywhere) would flatten a real severity difference.

correctedBlastRadius.note: 72 is the default rookie pool (DEFAULT_ROOKIES) and is really 'every player in the user's workspace' — the omission is per-player-universal, not limited to 72. Manifests only while myRemaining < myWinningBid; at the pristine state ($417 vs $69) every emitted number is affordable and the defect is invisible.

whatWouldSettleIt: Whether this is P0 or P1 turns on one UX question I cannot settle by code reading: does a mid-auction user read the 'Win at' cell or the 'My remaining' card first. A five-user session on /draft with a spent-down workspace would settle it. The code defect itself needs nothing further — there is no min(..., myRemaining) term anywhere in draft-logic.js.

reasoning:
The observations re-run and are true. The conclusion built on them does not follow, and its sharpest specific claim is falsified by experiment.

WHAT SURVIVES (all re-verified): the four constant-tuning reports do all optimize mean absolute change in canonicalConsensusRank (backtest_blend_params.md:6, alpha_lambda:'Metric: value-weighted rank change', alpha_shrinkage, percentile_reference_n, soft_fallback). backtest_blend_params.md:8 really does say 'Lower = more stable = probably better-calibrated' — an unearned inference in a committed report. MIN_FULL_COVERAGE_DEPTH=60 (src/canonical/idp_backbone.py:304) really has no backtest: `ls scripts/ | grep backtest` returns 10 scripts, none for coverage depth. And there is no forward-looking realized-outcome join for the market board.

WHAT DIES:

1. 'Three of five constants do not even match the recommendation their own report produced, WITH NO NOTE ANYWHERE SAYING WHY.' False for all three. alpha: data_contract.py:5375-5395 is an 18-line comment naming the alpha=0 stability optimum, calling it 'product-bad' verbatim, citing docs/architecture/optimization-target.md, and stating the chosen cell (alpha=0.10, lambda=0.10, VW 0.299) as 'the cheapest non-degenerate joint point'. lambda: :5402-5429 documents the 2026-04-20 retirement and the reason (double-damping on the same signal). N: :5297-5303 gives the structural reason ('500 aligns with KTC's native pool'), echoed in CLAUDE.md. The finding read the standalone reports and not the constants.

2. 'N ships 500 against its own 400 recommendation' — I tested whether 400 is actually the better value under the repo's DECLARED target. tests/canonical/test_ktc_reconciliation.py imports _PERCENTILE_REFERENCE_N; with N=400 it fails 9 of 13, blowing the pinned tolerance bands (rank 200 at -20.4pp against a +/-10pp band, rank 400 value 996 -> 794). N=500 is not unexplained drift from a recommendation — it is the value that satisfies an enforced gate the churn metric does not measure. Adopting the finding's implied fix would break production calibration.

3. 'stability was adopted as a proxy and then read as if it were the target' — the opposite is documented. docs/architecture/optimization-target.md declares 'market consensus fit' with per-rank tolerance bands (+/-2pp ranks 1-50, +/-3pp 100-150, +/-10pp 200-400), pinned in the test above, and has a section 'What this target is NOT optimizing for' whose first bullet is 'Predictive accuracy on future trades — that would require a labeled trade corpus we don't have.' src/model_registry/holdout.py:26-41 says the same in its own docstring ('It does NOT measure accuracy against reality... Anyone citing these numbers must say which of those two claims they are making'). The alpha comment invokes that declared target BY NAME to reject the stability optimum. A repo that names its proxy, states its limits, and overrides the proxy when it conflicts with the declared target is not one that mistook the proxy for the target.

4. numericProof is invalid as constructed. expected=5 ('every shipped value equals its report's recommendation') is not a defensible expectation when the joint report — the later, authoritative one — explicitly instructs the reader NOT to take the standalone optima (alpha >= ~0.05, lambda >= ~0.05). Live alpha=0.10 SATISFIES that guidance, so the '1 of 5' count is wrong on its own terms.

5. Status and severity. No wrong number is demonstrated anywhere. blastRadius 1092 players / 100 routes / 38 pages is 'the whole board depends on the blend', which is trivially true of any constant and is not defect impact. Rescoping to P3 documentation/methodology hygiene, scoped to what actually survives: one overclaiming sentence in backtest_blend_params.md:8, three of four reports printing 'Promote X' without carrying the joint report's caveat, one genuinely untuned constant (MIN_FULL_COVERAGE_DEPTH=60), and the absence of a realized-outcome validation the repo already documents as unavailable. Note also that scripts/backtest_mad_lambda.py is cited at data_contract.py:5414 and does not exist in scripts/ — a separate small defect the finding did not catch.

correctedBlastRadius.note: No player value is shown to be wrong. Corrected scope is documentation + one untuned constant: 1 overclaiming line (reports/backtest_blend_params.md:8), 3 reports whose 'Promote' lines omit the joint report's own caveat, 1 constant with no backtest (src/canonical/idp_backbone.py:304, affecting exactly 3 registered sources at depth 50 per the finding's own coverage-weight-live.json), and 1 dangling script reference (data_contract.py:5414 -> scripts/backtest_mad_lambda.py, absent).

whatWouldSettleIt: The residual true claim — no forward-looking outcome validation for the market board — would be settled by running the existing machinery (scripts/backtest_adjusted_board.py's realized-scoring join, or src/model_registry/board_holdout.py) against alpha/lambda/N and reporting whether the accuracy optimum differs from the shipped values. Until someone does that, 'the constants are wrong' is unsupported; only 'the constants are unvalidated against outcomes, which the repo says out loud' is supported.
